title: NormScore with SummarizedExperiment and NormalyzedDE

code: assayNames(se) colnames(se) colData(se)  rawData <- assay(se, "Unnormalized")  normalizationMethods <- c("Mean", "Median", "Quantile")  normalizedDataList <- lapply(     normalizationMethods,     function(method) assay(se, method) ) names(normalizedDataList) <- normalizationMethods  groupData <- data.frame(     Samples = colnames(se),     Groups = as.character(colData(se)$group) )  normScoreResults <- normScore(     normalizedDataList = normalizedDataList,     groupData = groupData,     rawData = rawData )  metadata(se)$normScore <- normScoreResults

title: Getting started with normScore
text: normScore provides tools evaluate rank normalization methods omics data using composite multi-metric scoring framework. package designed help compare different normalization strategies based several complementary criteria, including variability, correlation structure, MA-trend behavior, relative log expression consistency, sample-level intensity consistency. vignette, show minimal workflow using simulated data.

title: Getting started with normScore
text: keep package lightweight reproducible, normScore includes data simulation function generates proteomics-like two-group datasets. simulated object contains three main elements: logData: simulated data log2 scale rawData: simulated data raw scale metadata: sample annotation group membership can inspect sample metadata:
code: library(normScore)  simData <- simulateData(     nProteins = 500,     nPerGroup = 4,     sampleShiftSd = 0.12,     sampleShiftCap = 1,     sampleSdStrength = 1.2,     sampleSdRho = 0.3,     rhoWithin = 0.6,     rhoBetween = 0.3,     loadingSd = 0.45,     sigmaHi = 0.03,     sigmaLo = 0.4,     gammaSigma = 3.8,     kMnar = 1.6,     addMissing = FALSE,     seed = 123 ) names(simData) #> [1] "logData"  "rawData"  "metadata" head(simData$metadata) #>   Samples Groups #> 1    G1_1     G1 #> 2    G1_2     G1 #> 3    G1_3     G1 #> 4    G1_4     G1 #> 5    G2_1     G2 #> 6    G2_2     G2

what: Building a list of normalized datasets
title: Getting started with normScore
text: main function package, normScore(), expects named list normalized datasets. element list matrix data frame rows (features) columns (samples). illustration purposes, create simple variants simulated log-scale data. real analysis, correspond different normalization methods.
code: # Median normalization MedianMat <- NormalyzerDE::medianNormalization(simData$rawData) colnames(MedianMat) <- colnames(simData$rawData) rownames(MedianMat) <- rownames(simData$rawData)  # Quantile normalization QuantileMat <- limma::normalizeQuantiles(     simData$logData ) colnames(QuantileMat) <- colnames(simData$logData) rownames(QuantileMat) <- rownames(simData$logData)   # CyclicLoess normalization CyclicNorm <- limma::normalizeCyclicLoess(     simData$logData, method="fast",  adaptive.span=FALSE )   # All together normalizedDataList <- list(     Log = simData$logData,     Median = MedianMat,     Quantile = QuantileMat,      CyclicLoess = CyclicNorm )  names(normalizedDataList) #> [1] "Log"         "Median"      "Quantile"    "CyclicLoess"

title: Getting started with normScore
text: now compute normalization ranking.
code: result <- normScore(     normalizedDataList = normalizedDataList,     groupData = simData$metadata,     rawData = simData$rawData,     returnDetails = TRUE,     nBoot = 150 ) #> Reference group set to G2. #> Alternative group set to G1.

title: Getting started with normScore
text: finalRanking element contains final composite score normalization method. Lower values indicate better normalization performance according scoring framework implemented package.
code: result$finalRanking #>    Quantile CyclicLoess      Median         Log  #>   0.2166984   1.3760648   2.7910586   5.9883198

title: Getting started with normScore
text: detailRanking element contains scaled item-wise scores used build final ranking. six item scores correspond : pooled coefficient variation within-group sample correlation MA-plot trend deviation mean-SD trend deviation RLE consistency total intensity consistency scaled combined final score.

text: Normalization critical step quantitative omics data analysis. Different normalization methods can alter structure data different ways, affecting downstream results differential analysis, sample clustering, fold-change estimation. normScore package provides composite scoring framework compare normalization methods using multiple complementary criteria. Rather relying single summary metric, normScore integrates different aspects normalization performance unified ranking.

what: Rank Normalization Methods Using a Composite Scoring Framework — normScore
title: Rank Normalization Methods Using a Composite Scoring Framework — normScore
text: Computes composite score rank normalization methods based multiple quality metrics derived normalized data matrices. function evaluates normalization method using six criteria: pooled coefficient variation (PCV), within-group sample correlation, MA-plot trend deviation, mean-SD trend deviation, relative log expression (RLE) consistency, total intensity consistency. metrics scaled, combined final score, used rank normalization methods. addition, correction factor derived coefficient variation raw sample intensities applied "Log" normalization method. Optionally, bootstrap resampling used estimate mean composite scores percentile-based confidence intervals.

title: Rank Normalization Methods Using a Composite Scoring Framework — normScore
text: function computes following six item scores normalization method: Item1: mean pooled coefficient variation across groups (PVC). Item2: within-group Spearman correlation summary, transformed lower values indicate better performance (Correlation). Item3: shape-corrected area-based deviation expected MA trend (logFC = 0), based MAplot. Item4: area-based deviation mean-SD trend horizontality, based meanSD plot. Item5: RLE-based mean absolute percentage error relative 1. Item6: quantile-based total intensity consistency metric. item scaled range 0 1 using min-max scaling summed total score. Lower scores indicate better normalization performance. correction factor based coefficient variation total raw sample intensities applied normalization method named "Log". returnDetails = FALSE, bootstrap resampling six item scores performed.results can visualized using plotBootstrapNormScore.
